newsitem.title: INDIA: Five trapped in collapsed Indian mine feared dead.
newsitem.headline: Five trapped in collapsed Indian mine feared dead.

text.p: Rescue workers used shovels and pickaxes on Wednesday to dig through the rubble of a collapsed mine in northern India in which officials said four people died and five were trapped and feared dead.
"The chances of their survival are most remote and we are now trying to recover their bodies," said V.K. Gupta, a senior official of the Jammu and Kashmir state government.
The mine caved in during the lunch break on Monday in Rajouri district, 133 km (83 miles) from Jammu, the winter capital of the Himalayan state.
"It was so sudden that everybody was taken unawares," mine manager Lala Jee Koul told Reuters. "Listening to the screams for help, we rushed inside the mine and extricated four charred bodies.
"Had the incident taken place half an hour earlier, it could have been a big disaster. Over 125 workers could have been trapped inside," Koul said.
Gupta said the narrow, two-km (1.2-mile) mine caved in at least three places. The five people trapped inside could be buried under the debris or could have died from asphyxiation, he said.
Bhagat Singh, one of 13 injured, said he heard a long hiss, followed by an explosion and fire.
Gupta said exploding methane gas pockets within the mine or sabotage could have triggered the collapse. The state government on Tuesday appointed a team to investigate.
Six of the mine's workers were abducted by suspected separatist guerrillas last week.
